topic: Fewer people, less noise, more room
title: Fewer people, less noise, more room
pt: Foco da aula: less / fewer / much / many: comparação de quantidade

solo90.name: Pausa

lines.en: Bia, I love this park on weekdays. There are fewer people, less noise and much more room to walk.
lines.pt: Bia, adoro este parque nos dias úteis. Há menos gente, menos barulho e muito mais espaço para caminhar.

lines.en: True. On Saturdays there are far too many people, and there is too much traffic near the entrance.
lines.pt: Verdade. Aos sábados há gente demais, e há trânsito demais perto da entrada.

lines.en: Last summer, fewer visitors came because it was so hot, but this year there are many more joggers.
lines.pt: No verão passado vieram menos visitantes porque fazia muito calor, mas este ano há muito mais corredores.

lines.en: I try to run less often now. I used to run every day, but I have fewer free hours.
lines.pt: Tento correr com menos frequência agora. Eu corria todo dia, mas tenho menos horas livres.

lines.en: That is normal. I spend much less time here than before, since I have more work and fewer holidays.
lines.pt: É normal. Passo muito menos tempo aqui do que antes, já que tenho mais trabalho e menos feriados.

lines.en: Still, how much time do you need to feel relaxed? I find that an hour is much better than nothing.
lines.pt: Mesmo assim, de quanto tempo você precisa para relaxar? Acho que uma hora é muito melhor que nada.

lines.en: An hour is enough. I bring less food and fewer bags now, and I enjoy the lake much more.
lines.pt: Uma hora basta. Levo menos comida e menos bolsas agora, e aproveito muito mais o lago.

lines.en: How many people usually swim in the pool at noon in summer? It looks quite crowded to me.
lines.pt: Quantas pessoas costumam nadar na piscina ao meio-dia no verão? Para mim parece bem lotada.

lines.en: Far too many. The water has less space, and fewer lifeguards are working on weekdays, so it can be risky.
lines.pt: Gente demais. A água tem menos espaço, e menos salva-vidas trabalham nos dias úteis, então pode ser arriscado.

lines.en: Then let us come early tomorrow. There will be less noise, fewer bikes and much cooler water.
lines.pt: Então vamos vir cedo amanhã. Haverá menos barulho, menos bicicletas e água muito mais fresca.

lines.en: Deal. I will bring a book. I have read many pages already, but not as much as I should.
lines.pt: Combinado. Vou trazer um livro. Já li muitas páginas, mas não tanto quanto deveria.

facts.sub: fewer people, less noise, much more room, how many.

facts.label: fewer + contável
facts.sub: Use fewer com contáveis no plural: fewer people, fewer bikes, fewer holidays. There are fewer people on weekdays. Fewer é o oposto de more para coisas que podemos contar.

facts.label: less + incontável
facts.sub: Use less com incontáveis: less noise, less time, less food. There is less noise here. Less é o oposto de more para coisas que não contamos.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Fewer is used with countable nouns.

items.why: In careful English we say fewer people.

items.s: Much is used with uncountable nouns.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Fewer is used with countable nouns. → Verdadeiro (Yes: fewer people.)
We say “less people”. → Falso (In careful English we say fewer people.)
Much is used with uncountable nouns. → Verdadeiro (Yes: much noise.)

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 2/2

items.s: Many is used with uncountable nouns.
The more you walk, the better you feel is correct.

pages.instruction: Mais uma rodada: decida e explique.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Many is used with uncountable nouns. → Falso (Many goes with countable nouns.)
The more you walk, the better you feel is correct. → Verdadeiro (It is a parallel comparative.)

pages.title: A calm morning in the park · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a bright morning in Austin. Fay walks along a path in the park. Tall trees give a little shade. A few joggers pass by slowly. Bia waits for her near the lake. The two friends start to talk.

“Bia, I love this park on weekdays. There are fewer people, less noise and much more room to walk.” says Fay. “True. On Saturdays there are far too many people, and there is too much traffic near the entrance.” says Bia. “Last summer, fewer visitors came because it was so hot, but this year there are many more joggers.” says Fay.

An hour is enough. I bring less food and fewer bags now, and I enjoy the lake much more.

You

Fay

You

Fay
